prompt.title: Make small promises and keep them
prompt.text: Pick one small thing you'll do, and by when. Then come back and say whether you did it. Small promises, kept, add up.
prompt.glossText: The book calls a promise you make and keep a commitment. Keeping them builds what it calls integrity.
prompt.whyItMatters: Each time you keep your word, you trust yourself a bit more. That trust is what lets you take on bigger things later. Start with promises you're sure you can keep.

list.empty: No promises yet. Start with one you can keep by tomorrow.
list.emptyFilter: No promises here. Pick another filter.

form.textPrompt: What's one small thing you'll do, for sure?
form.textPlaceholder: e.g. Call Mum on Sunday afternoon.
form.dueDatePrompt: When will it be done? Soon is better.
form.repairNotePrompt: What got in the way, and how will you make it right?
form.repairNotePlaceholder: e.g. I underestimated it. I sent a draft on Monday and agreed a new date.

checklist.kept: Keep it, then mark it Kept

guide.inShort: You'll write down small promises and say whether you kept them. Two minutes to add one, a few seconds to tick it off. Over time you'll see how often your word holds.
howTo: Tap "Add promise" and write one small thing you'll do.
Say who it's to, and pick a date. Tomorrow beats next month.
When the day comes, tap Kept or Broken.
If it's Broken, write what got in the way and how you'll fix it.
Add a new promise as soon as one is done. Tap "Mark done" once you've kept one.

examples.title: Send the report to Dina by Friday.

fields.label: What got in the way
fields.value: "I underestimated it. I sent a draft on Monday and agreed a new date."

sample.text: Send the report to Dina by Friday.

guide.afterwards: Keep a promise every day of the 30-day test. When one breaks, fix it the same day and make the next one smaller. Your kept rate should climb; if it doesn't, shrink the promises, not the effort.
